title: [Refactor][310P] Avoid bool-mask IndexPut in GDN prefill state init
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?
In the 310P GDN prefill path, `_forward_core` uses two indexed assignments on
the recurrent state for every layer. On Ascend both of them lower to the
generic IndexPut implementation, which is pure operator overhead in this layer;
the boolean-mask form additionally has to convert the mask into an index
tensor before writing.

This PR replaces both with equivalent dedicated operators:

- Clearing the initial state of requests without history:
  `initial_state[~has_initial_state, ...] = 0` -> `masked_fill_` with a
  broadcast mask. One element-wise kernel, no mask-to-index materialization,
  and exactly the same positions are cleared.
- Writing the final recurrent state back to the paged cache:
  `ssm_state[indices] = ...` -> `index_copy_` on a flattened 2D view. A
  dedicated single-dimension copy instead of the generic multi-dimensional
  IndexPut template, writing the same rows to the same slots.

Both changes are bit-exact: the indices are unique per request, no accumulate
path is involved, and the dtype conversion and arithmetic are unchanged. There
is no API or behavior change outside this layer.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
No. The change only replaces how the 310P GDN prefill path clears and writes
back its recurrent state internally. The results are bit-exact, and there is no
change to public APIs, configuration options, kernel signatures, or the
behaviour of any non-310P backend.

### How was this patch tested?

- Accuracy: served Qwen3.5 on Atlas 300I Duo with both the baseline build and
  this patch, and compared the generated outputs over the same prompts; the
  results are identical.

- Profiling: collected a MindStudio trace of a prefill step and confirmed the
  two indexed assignments no longer take the generic IndexPut path.

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [ ] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: I reviewed whether this change involves
  boundary conditions (e.g. empty input, single/zero element, min/max values,
  off-by-one, sequence-length limits, integer overflow). Where applicable, I
  added unit tests covering these edge cases in `tests/ut/` or `tests/e2e/`.
- [ ] **Regression test**: If this PR fixes a bug, I added a regression test
  that would fail without the fix.
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: I covered abnormal paths (exceptions,
  timeouts, out-of-range, division by zero) in addition to the happy path.
- [ ] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: New tests assert real behavior and are
  not written merely to satisfy CI.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: If this PR touches a performance-sensitive path,
  I attached benchmark results and added performance regression tests.
